intro: Everything in the conversation (messages, tool results, file contents) counts toward the context limit. Managing it well keeps responses sharp in long sessions.

sections.title: Signs of a Full Context Window

items.title: Shorter, less precise responses
items.body: If Claude's answers start getting vague or generic, context is probably near the limit. Run /compact.

items.title: Forgetting earlier decisions
items.body: If Claude contradicts something decided earlier in the session, the context has been truncated.

items.title: Truncated tool results
items.body: Long file reads or command outputs may be cut off silently as the window fills.

items.desc: Compress conversation history into a dense summary, freeing space for more work
Keep specific context: append what to preserve after the command
items.example: /compact — keep the auth architecture decisions and reviewed file list

items.title: Reference, don't paste
items.body: Say 'see src/api/users.ts:42-78' rather than pasting the code. It costs tokens for both input and output.

items.title: Ask for concise outputs
items.body: Say 'give me just the list, no explanation needed' when you only need the fact, not the reasoning.

items.title: Summarise before continuing
items.body: After a long exploration: 'Summarise the key findings in 5 bullet points. We'll use that as our working context going forward.'

items.title: Start fresh for new tasks
items.body: When you've finished one task and starting something unrelated, start a new session. Carrying irrelevant history just wastes context.
